extracted.intended_audience: HHS rulemakers, agency policymakers, and small-entity stakeholders (including SBA Office of Advocacy)
extracted.subtask_description: Office of Advocacy public comments to HHS’ Request for Information on deregulation, identifying deregulatory opportunities and procedural reforms to reduce burdens on small entities across HHS programs (CMS, FDA, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider direct and indirect impacts of rules on small entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Agencies Should Consider the Direct and Indirect Impacts of their Rules on Small Entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To understand the true scope of a rule’s effects on small entities, agencies should consider a broader view of all relevant impacts, e.g., a regulation on a supplier may also impact all businesses that purchase the supplier’s products. Examine totality of the regulatory process rather than isolated provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and minimize paperwork burdens (Paperwork Reduction Act compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS should examine the paperwork burdens it currently impose on small entities and strive to minimize them consistent with the Paperwork Reduction Act (PRA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamline forms, clarify compliance steps, avoid duplicative information collections across federal agencies, and thoroughly review existing collections for ease of use. Note OMB/ICR inventories and quantify burden (e.g., HHS >1,100 active collections, 1.7 billion annual burden hours).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize and give appropriate consideration to Advocacy and small-entity input
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must give every appropriate consideration to comments provided by the Office of Advocacy; include a response to Advocacy comments in any explanation or discussion accompanying the final rule unless the agency certifies public interest is not served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize responses on deregulatory ideas proposed by small entities; conduct small-entity outreach before finalizing deregulatory or burdensome rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow RFA requirements: assess impacts and consider less-burdensome alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: For rules expected to have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities, agencies must assess impacts and consider less burdensome alternatives; if not significant, agencies may certify with factual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use RFA §603 analysis; support certifications with adequate factual basis; carry out SBREFA processes when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid one-size-fits-all percentage limits without small-entity exceptions (HCBS 80/20 rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HCBS rule requiring at least 80 percent of payments be allocated to direct care workers (leaving 20 percent for admin/overhead) may be unsustainable for small home care agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alternative approaches such as scaling thresholds based on provider size, rural/urban status, risk of closure, and/or an exceptions process for small providers; account for recordkeeping costs to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw or rework especially burdensome rules pending small-entity outreach (recommendation to withdraw CMS-2442-F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy recommends withdrawal of specific rules (e.g., CMS-2442-F) and additional small entity outreach to identify less-burdensome alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If stakeholders report significant unforeseen burdens (IT upgrades, reporting requirements), pause implementation and engage small entities to identify alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit and reform use of civil monetary penalties (CMPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMPs in healthcare settings are perceived as disproportionate, may not improve quality of care, and can divert funds from resident care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: Apply CMPs only where facility fails to submit a plan of correction and/or achieve substantial compliance; allow CMP fines to be used to correct deficient practices; establish standards related to survey timelines; eliminate delayed CMP notifications; establish a State Performance Standards System (SPSS) measure; eliminate use of CMPs for self-reported incidents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind or modify punitive provisions in SNF PPS rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Skilled Nursing Facilities Prospective Payment System rule’s punitive financial penalties should be rescinded or revised to avoid harming workforce investment and facility improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsider provisions that prevent facilities from conducting Nurse Aide Training and competency programs when CMPs exceed certain thresholds and identify duplicative enforcement provisions (e.g., multiple CMPs for same noncompliance, three-standard-survey lookback).

rubrics_metrics.name: End or make voluntary mandatory NHSN reporting for long-term care
rubrics_metrics.description: Discontinue mandatory National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) reporting for long-term care facilities and allow voluntary reporting because COVID-19 emergency has ended and reporting duplicates other systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: redundancy with MDS and local public health reporting, misalignment between NHSN definitions and ICD-10, large paperwork burden (ICR estimates), and data duplication leading to inefficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal or modify 42 CFR § 483.71 Facility Assessment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders suggest CMS should repeal the § 483.71 Facility Assessment requirement because it imposes administrative regulatory burden with little impact on resident care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removal would reduce paperwork burden and costs to nursing homes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve Informal Dispute Resolution (IDR/IIDR) processes for timeliness and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise IDR and IIDR to include regulatory clarifications and adjust timeframes to improve efficiency, transparency, and consistency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Align processes with a shorter resolution timeframe (e.g., 60 days); prevent premature uploading of survey results to CASPER until dispute resolution; provide facilities written rationales for final decisions; improve IDR reviewer knowledge to increase trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broaden qualifying experience for Director of Food and Nutritional Services (§483.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modify § 483.60 to increase availability of qualified Directors of Food and Nutritional Services by recognizing relevant work experience in other healthcare settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested language: allow 2+ years' experience in food and nutrition services in a nursing facility setting or other healthcare setting plus completion of food safety/management course covering topics like foodborne illness, sanitation, purchasing/receiving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind specific HCBS regulatory provisions prejudging settings
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders assert parts of the Home and Community-Based Settings (HCBS) rule are too restrictive, presumptively institutionalizing many settings and deterring Medicaid-serving residential care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend rescinding parts of 42 CFR (Part 441 and specified sections §441.301, §441.530, §441.710) that create heightened scrutiny and presumptions that limit options for seniors and people with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjust survey frequency for ICF/IID based on performance
rubrics_metrics.description: State Survey Agency currently must survey each ICF/IID facility no later than 15 months after prior survey; stakeholders recommend surveying high-performing ICFs less often (e.g., every 36 months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance-based surveying would optimize resource allocation, reduce administrative burden on compliant facilities, and align ICF survey cycles with hospitals, home health, and hospice (three-year cycle). Quantify cost savings where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce redundant respiratory illness reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: New acute respiratory illness reporting (e.g., weekly NHSN reporting) imposes reporting burden and duplicates other reporting mechanisms post-PHE; recommend discontinuing mandatory weekly reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons: COVID-19 emergency ended; vaccination and respiratory illness data reported via MDS and local public health; misalignment with ICD-10; estimate burdens (e.g., CMS estimated $12.6 million).

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Payroll-Based Journal (PBJ) reporting accurate and contestable
rubrics_metrics.description: PBJ policies are overly complex and do not allow providers to submit corrected or missing data, causing severe score penalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations: establish review/reconsideration and appeal processes modeled on SNF QRP Reconsideration policy; provide preview report after final submission and at least 14 business days to review and correct data; allow corrected PBJ data to be used in Value Based Purchasing measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit OASIS data collection to Medicare/Medicaid patients (rescind all-payer OASIS rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rescind the OASIS final rule that lifted suspension of home health OASIS data collection for all-payers beginning July 1, 2025; stakeholders request limiting reporting to patients for whom home health provider receives Medicare/Medicaid payments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: expanded collection increases direct and opportunity costs for providers (especially rural), and restricting to Medicare/Medicaid would significantly reduce burden (rule estimated $267 million reduction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Align face-to-face encounter and certification regulations with CARES Act (allow NPPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise §§ 424.22 and 484.4 to conform with CARES Act provisions expanding authority of non-physician practitioners (NPPs) to certify eligibility and order home health services and conduct face-to-face encounters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove regulatory language that limits face-to-face encounter to certifying physician/practitioner for community admissions and that requires NPP collaboration with physicians when statute provides flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow therapists to perform initial and comprehensive assessments when therapy is ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanently amend § 484.55(a)(2) and § 484.55(b)(2) to allow PTs, SLPs, and OTs to conduct initial and comprehensive assessments whenever therapy services are ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stakeholders note CMS waived these requirements during the PHE and request making that flexibility permanent to reduce burden and improve care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate/extend 96-hour CoP for critical access hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate or extend the 96-hour average length of stay Condition of Participation and remove the 96-hour physician certification CoP for critical access hospitals to provide rural flexibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: rural hospitals need flexibility to treat patients locally and handle system fluctuations without prohibitive certification constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow direct admission to rural hospital swing beds for qualifying Medicare patients
rubrics_metrics.description: Permit direct admission to swing bed care for Medicare patients who meet SNF requirements but do not require acute care, per 42 C.F.R. § 409.31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would allow timely access to appropriate care, avoid costly inpatient admissions, and save resources for providers and beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 3-day inpatient stay requirement for Medicare SNF coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate the historical 3-day hospital inpatient stay requirement (42 C.F.R. § 409.30) before Medicare will cover a SNF stay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing this provision would free up rural hospital capacity and allow appropriate transfer sooner, benefiting beneficiaries and constrained facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend site-neutral payment exemption to Medicare-Dependent Hospitals (MDHs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow Medicare-Dependent Hospitals to receive the same site-neutral payment policy exemptions currently afforded to rural Sole Community Hospitals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: MDHs serve as sole access points and may face higher patient volumes; exemption would prevent burdensome payment policy impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate mandatory CMMI models and return to voluntary experimentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders urge elimination of recently created mandatory CMMI participation requirements (e.g., TEAM, IOTA, EPM) and recommend returning to voluntary model testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns: mandatory models increase costs, exceed CMS’ testing mandate, and reduce stakeholder flexibility; prefer voluntary innovation laboratory approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: End IRF Review Choice Determinations (RCD) requiring 100% pre-payment review
rubrics_metrics.description: IRF RCD programs (e.g., 100% prior authorization in some states) impose administrative burden without apparent benefits given high approval rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend eliminating mandatory RCD expansions when they produce high approval and high administrative cost; adopt less burdensome documentation or review approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclude premium cigars from Very Low Nicotine and manufacturing standards rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Stakeholders ask FDA to exclude premium cigars from the Very Low Nicotine rule and the Tobacco Product Manufacturing Standards Rule because these regulations impose costs without demonstrated public health benefits for premium cigars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations include adopting a court-aligned definition of 'premium cigar' (multi-element definition provided), exempting premium cigars from inappropriate FDA regulation, protecting small businesses from unjustified regulatory costs, and ensuring stability for manufacturers/importers/retailers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop consistent cigar categories and research definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA should develop formal categories and definitions for cigars for use in research to ensure consistency among studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with other federal agencies to standardize categories and definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove 'written assurance' requirements absent explicit statutory basis (FSMA customer provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend rescinding requirements for annual/biannual 'written assurances' in FSMA-related customer provisions except where statute explicitly requires them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: written assurance requirements create massive expense, redundant compliance, and are especially burdensome for small entities in multilayered supply chains; FDA has applied enforcement discretion in the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite specific regulations for each Form 483 observation
rubrics_metrics.description: When issuing Form 483 inspectional observations, FDA inspectors should cite the specific regulation associated with each observation rather than omitting regulatory references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revise Inspections Operations Manual to require references to underlying cGMP regulations for each cGMP-related observation to improve transparency and enable rapid corrective action, especially for small businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exempt very small establishments from 21 CFR Part 111 (or apply enforcement discretion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocacy recommends exempting very small dietary supplement establishments (or apply formal enforcement discretion) from 21 CFR Part 111, using a threshold (e.g., <$250,000 in annual sales based on 3-year rolling average adjusted for inflation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions for discretion: (a) firm complies with local health regulations; (b) for processed ingredient purchases, firm obtains and reviews vendor certificates of analysis per lot; (c) botanical ingredients not in certain Safety Classes. Rationale: original cost estimates underestimated burdens on very small firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow master manufacturing records (MMR) to cover a range of batch sizes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 21 CFR § 111.205(a) to permit a master manufacturing record to cover a range of lot/batch sizes when proportions, equipment, in-process specs, and packaging remain the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternate language provided: MMR may cover range if reviewed/approved by quality control personnel prior to use; packaging MMR not required for every batch size if parameters don't vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit single-employee supplement manufacturing operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend 21 CFR § 111.210(h)(3)(ii) to avoid indirectly requiring a minimum of two people for manual operations so that facilities may operate with one employee where appropriate and modern verification systems exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested language modeled on infant formula cGMP provisions: allow one person with another person or system verifying weighing/adding operations; permit system verification to replace second-person requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stop imposing manufacturing cGMP requirements on 'own label distributors' absent notice-and-comment rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: FDA should discontinue the practice of treating own label distributors as subject to manufacturing cGMP obligations under Part 111 until formal rulemaking clarifies scope and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: preamble-based extra-regulatory standards lack notice-and-comment foundation, create duplicative documentation burdens, and raise statutory concerns under 21 U.S.C. 342(g); own-label distribution often enables market entry for small businesses.
